entries.title: Vigil held for 7-year-old girl killed in Chatham stabbing
entries.summary: <p>A vigil was held Sunday afternoon in Chatham to honor a young girl who was stabbed to death Saturday.</p><p>Family friends and community members gathered in the 8600 block of south Cottage Grove Avenue where 7-year-old Edi Mari Hernandez Chacon was killed.</p><p>Family members, dressed in black and white, released white balloons, lit candles and scattered candy at the spot where Edi Mari was police said a woman <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/03/woman-in-custody-after-girl-7-fatally-stabbed-in-chatham" target="_blank" >attacked the child Saturday morning</a>. The girl’s loved ones shed tears and embraced each other as they circled around the candles.</p><p>Edi Mari’s family declined to speak to a Sun-Times reporter.</p><p>“It’s really sad,” said Michelle Clark, who attended the vigil to show support for the family. “I’m a mother, and I can’t imagine the pain they must be going through.”</p><p>Edi Mari was walking with her older sister just before noon when a woman approached her and stabbed her multiple times in the back, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Bystanders who witnessed the stabbing intervened and detained the woman, police said.</p><p>The girl was taken to Comer Children’s Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.</p><p>The woman, who has not been identified, suffered injuries during the scuffle with bystanders, and she was transported to the hospital before being taken into police custody.</p><p>Clark said she had seen the woman several times at a nearby train station and cannot understand what may have led her to attack a young girl.</p><p>“We need to protect children,” she said. “They deserve to be safe walking down the street.”</p><p>Chicago police had not announced charges as of Sunday evening.</p><p>“I am deeply saddened by the senseless stabbing of a 7 year old child in our neighborhood,” Ald. Michelle Harris said in a statement. “My heart goes out to her family, friends, and everyone who is affected by this horrific incident. No child should ever have to experience violence or fear while simply walking down the sidewalk.”</p>
entries.author: Cindy Hernandez

entries.title: Bears RB Kyle Monangai bludgeons Jets in 23-12 win
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> running back Kyle Monangai was exhausted. His running mate, D’Andre Swift, was on the bench as punishment for fumbling. His right thumb hurt for some reason.</p><p>But he kept plowing forward, time after time after time. The Bears took over with 9:16 left in Sunday’s 23-12 win against the Jets at Soldier Field — and never gave the ball back.</p><p>Monangai touched the ball nine times on the drive — eight runs and one pass from fellow backup Tyson Bagent. He finished with 30 carries — the most by a Bears running back since David Montgomery had 32 in 2020 — for 146 yards.</p><p>Sunday was a boxing match in which the Bears threw nothing but jabs. Monangai served as Bears coach Ben Johnson’s left hand to bludgeon the Jets. Bagent, who took over this week as the Bears’ quarterback with Caleb Williams out, didn’t provide much of a right hook. He was solid, though, completing 25-of-34 passes — that’s 74% — for 268 yards, one interception and an 83.9 passer rating. </p><p>Not bad for a pair of second-stringers.</p><p>“We all know that we’re gonna run the football,” Monangai said. “We know it. The other team knows it. The people watching at home and in the stadium know it. … We put the time in to still stick to what we know we’re going to do. We just say, ‘You gotta come stop this.’”</p><p>The Jets could not. The Bears finished with a franchise-best 34 first downs to the Jets’ seven. They averaged a first down every 2.6 plays. They held the ball for all but 17 minutes, 15 seconds, and never punted. In the fourth quarter alone, they held the ball for all but 45 seconds.</p><p>“That’s just who we are,” tight end Cole Kmet said. “That’s our team. I think our run game and how we are at the line of scrimmage is something that can carry over throughout the entire season. Despite who we have under center, I think it shows we can beat anybody when we’re physical up front.”</p><p>Johnson marveled at Monangai’s physicality. On a day in which the Bears struggled in the red zone, he had their only two touchdowns, a one-yard, second-effort plunge on fourth down in the first quarter and a five-yarder in the third.</p><p>“That’s just one ball of muscle right there,” defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo said.</p><p>Johnson didn’t realize he gave Monangai a career-high 30 carries — it was as many as he’d had all season before Sunday — until he got back into his Soldier Field office.</p><p>“He ran really hard,” Johnson said. “He found some creases and turned on the gas. I thought I saw one really, really good stiff arm there as well.</p><p>“When you see a guy running like that, you want to feed him as the play caller. And I do think it elevates all of those guys out there and gives them a spark as well, the guy's blocking for him. And it was good to see. We needed that.”</p><p>Whether sparked by Monangai or the below-average play of the opposition, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/04/chicago-bears-defense-jets-ben-johnson-tyson-bagent-kyle-monangai-dillon-thieneman-geno-smith-isaiah-williams" target="_blank" >Bears’ defense dominated</a>, giving up seven first downs on eight possessions. Four of the Jets’ eight drives went for six yards or less. Swift ran inspired, too, totaling 58 yards on 15 carries. His third-quarter fumble at the Bears’ 28 kept the Jets in the game — they’d kick a field goal to pull within seven — and got the running back benched the rest of the way. Roschon Johnson had four carries from then on to fill in for Monangai.</p><p>The Bears are the NFL’s best rushing team, and Swift and Monangai the best running back duo. They’re the seventh NFL duo since 1950 — and the first since 1976 — to each have at least 300 rushing yards through the season’s first four games.</p><p>“Keep the defense off the field,” right tackle Darnell Wright said. “Control the football. … Put it in our hands. Good results.”</p><p>After 38-year-old third-stringer Case Keenum captured the sport’s imagination Monday night, Johnson refused to publicly name a starting quarterback. When Keenum found out it would be Bagent, he wanted to be the one to tell him — and did at Halas Hall on Wednesday morning after asking him to come into work early.</p><p>“Tyson's earned the right to be our No. 2 quarterback,” Johnson said. “I have a lot of confidence in him, thought he played really well today. Efficient with the football.”</p><p>The one exception: when he threw a second-quarter interception to Minkah Fitzpatrick, who ended the Jets’ NFL-record 21-game streak without an interception.</p><p>Bagent wasn’t technically the starter — Johnson put Keenum at quarterback and split Bagent wide on the first play of the game. Keenum pitched the ball to Swift and left the game for good, with the coach later describing it as akin to the ceremonial first pitch. That was the only detail that kept the Bears from becoming the first team since the 1997 Jaguars to have three starting quarterbacks win a game in the first four weeks of the season. </p><p>Barring a quick return from Williams, Bagent lines up to make next week’s start in Green Bay. Whether he’ll have Monangai by his side depends on the running back’s right thumb; he had imaging done after the game, and the Bears figure to give him a diagnosis Monday. Monangai didn't seem too concerned.</p><p>Either way, the Bears' run game will travel.</p><p>“For everybody, it's pretty easy to get excited and juiced up for that one,” Bagent said. “Which, I'm sure, they will be, too.”</p>

entries.title: Vikings stay unbeaten, top winless Dolphins 15-10
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS — The Minnesota Vikings stayed undefeated with more dominance by their defense and five field goals from Will Reichard, sidestepping their early passing game problems to secure a 15-10 victory over the winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday.</p><p>T.J. Hockenson had a career-high-tying 13 receptions for 119 yards on 13 targets from Kyler Murray, including the game-sealing 8-yard catch on third-and-5 from the 10. Hockenson was wide open and could've coasted into the end zone, but he wisely slid in front of the goal line to drain the clock down to the two-minute warning.</p><p>With the Dolphins out of timeouts, the Vikings had Murray take three straight kneel-downs to move to 4-0 for the second time in three years.</p><p>The Dolphins, who are 0-4 for the first time since 2019 in their first season under coach Brian Flores, were crushed by a combination of unforced mistakes and a bit of bad luck.</p><p>New Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis went just 9 for 17 for 85 yards, losing a fumble during one of the two sacks by Dallas Turner. Willis thought he had escaped the relentless Vikings pass rush to float a 68-yard touchdown pass to Chris Bell early in the second quarter, but Bell was flagged for illegal touching after stepping out of bounds as he moved to get open while Willis scrambled toward the sideline.</p><p>The Vikings had 11 penalties for 85 yards, but they dodged a costly flag when Ivan Pace Jr. had a call for roughing the kicker waved off when the video replay assist system determined he tipped Bradley Pinion's punt and therefore didn't commit a penalty.</p><p>After netting just 76 yards on 21 plays in the first half and failing to finish any possession across midfield, the Dolphins finally found a couple of creases in Minnesota's otherwise-suffocating defense directed by Flores, who's in his fourth year as coordinator.</p><p>Ollie Gordon, in an elevated role following the season-ending knee injury to star running back De'Vone Achane, ripped off a career-long 53-yard run on third-and-5 to set up Riley Patterson's 27-yard field goal. Gordon had a 12-yard touchdown run on the next drive to pull the Dolphins within 12-10 late in the third quarter.</p><p>Reichard, who stretched the NFL's longest active streak to 31 consecutive made field goals, drew a loud roar from the otherwise restless crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium when he was shown on the videoboard during the two-minute warning.</p><p>Murray finished 27 for 37 for 247 yards without a turnover, but he took four sacks for 34 yards against a Dolphins defense that had none in the first three games and was often tentative and unsteady in the pocket until Hockenson helped him open up the field with a handful of clutch and difficult catches.</p><p>Aaron Jones also carried another heavy load with 20 carries for 94 yards and four receptions for 34 yards, with the Vikings missing star wide receiver Justin Jefferson (ankle) for the first time since Week 12 of the 2023 season and running back Jordan Mason (thumb) for the third game in a row.</p><h3>Injury report</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Miami:</b> Starting safety Dante Trader (knee) was hurt in the second quarter and returned after halftime.</p><p><b>Minnesota:</b> LG Donovan Jackson (knee) was sidelined in the first quarter. LT Christian Darrisaw (neck) was hurt in the second quarter after going head-first into the pile at the end of a run, returning after halftime only to be pulled again in the fourth quarter for concussion evaluation.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p>Miami hosts Cincinnati next Sunday.</p><p>Minnesota plays at New Orleans next Sunday.<br></p>
